issues.description: IAM-policy fetch failure silently degrades to publicly_shared=False, producing false-negative PASS findings
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (permission denied, transient error), _get_images logs and sets publicly_shared=False, so the check reports PASS for images whose sharing state is actually unknown. A security tool must not coerce 'unknown' into 'safe'. Introduce a tri-state or explicit error finding so PASS means verified-not-public.

issues.description: Check name is inconsistent between PR description/CHANGELOG references and the shipped artifacts
issues.detail: Shipped metadata, paths, and class use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, but the PR description references compute_image_publicly_shared. The check identifier is the contract callers and dashboards bind to; the negation-in-name versus positive publicly_shared field also invites mis-reasoning. Pick one name and propagate everywhere before merge.

issues.description: Image ADT bakes the check verdict into a derived boolean and discards binding evidence
issues.detail: publicly_shared is a precomputed boolean; the bindings (roles, members) that justified it are dropped at service-construction time. Storing the raw public members or bindings on the Image would let remediation, audit logs, and future checks reason about which role grants public access without re-querying.

issues.description: Public-member detection is complected with the listing/pagination loop
issues.detail: _get_images interleaves project iteration, pagination, per-image IAM fetch, error handling, and the allAuthenticatedUsers scan. The bindings-to-bool transform is pure; extracting _is_publicly_shared(iam_policy) would flatten the listing loop into a filter and let the rule be tested directly without API mocks.

issues.description: Tests pin mocked outputs rather than exercising the bindings-to-flag transformation
issues.detail: Service tests assert publicly_shared values that the getIamPolicy stubs pre-decide, and check tests construct Image objects with publicly_shared already set. The permission-denied case is asserted as publicly_shared=False, locking in the leaky behavior. Extract the scan as a pure function and test it directly on binding dicts.

synthesis.summary: The check follows the existing GCP service/check pattern and works on the happy path, but the panel converges on two contract problems. First, an IAM-policy fetch failure is silently coerced into publicly_shared=False, so PASS no longer means "verified not public" — a dangerous value/identity confusion in a security tool. Second, the check name is inconsistent between the PR description and the shipped artifacts, and the negative name reads a positive field. Underneath, the Image ADT collapses the rule into a derived boolean and drops the bindings that justified it, the listing loop complects I/O with a pure transform, and tests largely verify the mocks. No correctness blockers beyond the failure-path semantics; structural cleanups would make the check honest, testable, and reusable.
